sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen on which the species is based — consists of an incomplete skeleton that includes limb bones, a fused series of vertebrae called the synsacrum, the pelvis, the shoulder girdle, and other vertebrae.
The spur on the male’s leg is unusually long for the animal’s overall size.
Eopavo inhabited a high-elevation savanna, a habitat unlike the humid forests favored by today’s peafowl.
Fossils of Eopavo were recovered from the Liushu Formation in China.
The genus is known from a single species, Eopavo hezhengensis, which is represented by a partial skeleton.
The animal lived during the Miocene epoch.
Its relatively small body size may have been an adaptation to the high-elevation savanna environment.
The elongated spur suggests that males could have engaged in aggressive physical contact, similar to some modern relatives.
Researchers propose that the peafowl lineage likely originated on the Tibetan Plateau.
Eopavo belongs to the clade Pavonini, which also contains the living genera Pavo and Afropavo.
Its remains come from late Miocene deposits in the Linxia Basin, near the edge of the Tibetan Plateau.
The scattered modern distribution of peafowl in southern Asia and central Africa fuels ongoing discussions about the clade’s geographic origin and evolutionary history.
